title: .LLab Sound™ Live Night Quest
intro: Plan a live night, a rave, a show or a community event, through The IV Phases™: what it is for, who owns what, how the night runs, and what lasts after it.

nodes.section: Phase I — What the night is for
nodes.prompt: What is this night for, and what should people feel and remember when it ends?

nodes.section: Phase I — What the night is for
nodes.prompt: Who is the night for first, and who else does it serve: the artists, the crew, the venue and the community around it?

nodes.section: Phase I — What the night is for
nodes.prompt: What are your non-negotiables: the standards you will not trade away for money or crowd size?

Who owns each part: programming and music, sound, lighting and visuals, staging and power, security and crowd safety, welfare and medical, ticketing and door, vendors, volunteers? Name one owner for each.
Which permits, licenses, insurance and venue agreements does the night need, and who holds them? (Check the rules where you are.)
What does the night cost, what comes in, and what is your break-even?
How do people get in and move: ticketing, the door, your capacity limit, crowd flow, and entry and exit routes?
What is the run-of-show: doors, sets, changeovers and curfew, and who calls each cue?
What is your sound and visuals plan: the system, power and backup, sound check, volume limits and hearing safety?
What is your safety and welfare plan: water, a quiet space, medical help, heat, crowd crush, alcohol and drugs as the law and venue require, and how a problem is reported and who acts?
How will your team communicate on the night, who makes which decisions, and what happens when the plan breaks?
What will you record afterward: numbers, what worked, what did not, incidents and lessons?
How will you thank and keep the artists, crew, venue and community, and what do you owe them after the night?
What will you write down so someone else could run the next one: contacts, contracts, cue sheets and load-in plans?
What would make this night part of something lasting: a series, a collective, a name someone else could carry on?
